Automation Opportunity: - Tracking auto-monitored; exceptions auto-flagged at threshold; ETA auto-pushed to store
Controls: - CTL-398 (delivery-tracking integrity — links to VS-06); operational: Logistics Manager escalation on exceptions
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tracking-blind-spot risk**: a delivery enters a GPS dead-zone (tunnel, remote province) and tracking goes dark; mitigated by the last-known-position + ETA-estimate fallback
- **Exception-overload risk**: too many minor exceptions (5-min delays) desensitize the Coordinator; mitigated by the >30-min threshold for exception-flagging
System Touchpoints: - Telematics/tracking (links to VS-06 / W199 fleet telematics, VS-56 / W2191 integration) — the real-time GPS tracking
- Alerting (links to VS-27 / W380) — the exception auto-alert
- Store comms (links to VS-07 / W571) — the ETA notification to stores
Time Estimate: Real-time monitoring absorbed into Logistics Coordinator role (~4 hours/day).

steps.activity: System tracks all 3PL deliveries: driver location, ETA, status; Coordinator monitors exceptions (delays >30 min, no-show, breakdown, route deviation); auto-alerts store of ETA
Store confirms receipt; exceptions escalated to Logistics Manager for corrective action

Automation Opportunity: - SLA auto-computed daily; breaches auto-flagged with root-cause-suggestion
Controls: - CTL-398 (SLA-accuracy — links to VS-56); operational: Logistics Manager daily sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **SLA-target-unrealistic risk**: the SLA is set tighter than the logistics reality (Philippine traffic, archipelago), causing chronic breaches that demoralize; mitigated by the SLA calibrated to the actual logistics capability
- **Breach-without-correction risk**: breaches are reported but the root cause isn't fixed; mitigated by the root-cause analysis and the partner-CAP (W2196)
System Touchpoints: - SLA engine (links to VS-56 / W2196 scorecard, VS-60 / W2292 fulfillment SLA) — the daily SLA computation
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the SLA-breach dataset
- Partner scorecard (links to VS-56 / W2196) — the SLA feeds the scorecard

steps.activity: System calculates daily SLA compliance by partner, DC, route, store; Coordinator investigates breaches (traffic, weather, capacity, dispatch delay); implements corrections

Automation Opportunity: - Partner auto-assigned; SLA auto-tracked; delay-customer auto-notified; failed-delivery auto-rescheduled
Controls: - CTL-398 (home-delivery SLA — links to VS-60); CTL-44 (delivery-record integrity); operational: CS supervisor sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Failed-delivery risk**: the customer isn't home for the delivery (no prior appointment); mitigated by the delivery-appointment confirmation (SMS/app) before dispatch
- **Provincial-SLA-miss risk**: the 3–5 day provincial SLA is missed due to inter-island logistics; mitigated by the SLA calibrated and the proactive customer communication
System Touchpoints: - Order routing (links to VS-60 / W2286, W548 on-demand) — the partner assignment
- SLA tracking (links to VS-60 / W2292, VS-56 / W2199) — the home-delivery SLA
- Customer comms (links to VS-13 / W56 backorder notification) — the proactive delay communication

steps.activity: System assigns to optimal partner by location/size/cost; tracks 2-day Metro / 3–5 day provincial SLA; proactively contacts customers for delays; failed deliveries rescheduled within 24 hours

fields.Participants: Receiving Clerk, Store Manager, Logistics Manager

Controls: - CTL-24: receiving-fraud detection; CTL-75 (damage-claim detection & recovery — links to VS-90); operational: Store Manager weekly sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Damage-not-detected risk**: the Clerk accepts a delivery without noticing hidden damage, losing the claim window; mitigated by the inspection-standard and the damage-photo evidence

- **Chronic-damage-partner risk**: a partner consistently damages deliveries, but the pattern isn't seen because each delivery's damage is handled as a one-off; mitigated by the weekly quality-issue report aggregating per-partner damage rates
System Touchpoints: - GR/inspection (links to VS-04 / W3 receiving, W109 store-level receiving) — the delivery inspection and GR
- Damage claims (links to VS-90 / W90 damage claims, VS-56 / W2196 scorecard) — the damage-record routing
- POD (links to VS-56 / W2202) — the damage notation on POD
Time Estimate: ~12 min/delivery × ~450/day = **~90 hours/day** Receiving Clerks (distributed across stores, absorbed into receiving).

steps.activity: Clerk inspects: damage, count vs. manifest, item condition; records GR; damaged items photographed, noted on POD, damage record created and routed to damage-claim handling process
Weekly: Store Manager reports quality issues; patterns by partner or route investigated

Automation Opportunity: - POD fully digital (signature + GPS + timestamp); auto-matched to settlement
Controls: - CTL-398 (ensure controlled execution — Delivery Performance & SLA Management (PA-56.2).)
- operational: POD integrity; delivery-fraud detection; operational: Logistics Coordinator settlement-match review
Pain Points / Risks: - **POD-fraud risk**: a driver forges a POD (delivers to the wrong location, signs for an undelivered item); mitigated by the GPS + timestamp + digital-signature triangulation

- **POD-lost risk**: a POD isn't captured (system failure, driver forgot), leaving the delivery unverifiable for settlement; mitigated by the no-POD-no-settlement rule (the partner can't bill without a POD)
System Touchpoints: - POD system (links to VS-56 / W2191 integration, VS-06 / W199 telematics) — the digital POD capture
- Settlement (links to VS-56 / W2206 invoice) — the POD auto-matched for settlement
- GR (links to VS-04 / W3) — the POD reconciled to the GR

steps.activity: Driver obtains POD: digital signature + GPS + timestamp; system stores with delivery record; auto-matches for settlement

Automation Opportunity: - Exception auto-categorized; resolution auto-suggested; customer auto-notified
Controls: - CTL-398 (exception-management accuracy); CTL-24 (exception-pattern fraud detection); operational: Logistics Manager exception-rate review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Exception-cascade risk**: an exception triggers a re-delivery that also fails (the root cause persists); mitigated by the exception-depth-limit and the root-cause fix
- **Customer-experience-degradation risk**: each exception adds delay and erodes trust; mitigated by the exception-rate target (<5–8%) and the root-cause fix
System Touchpoints: - Exception management (links to VS-60 / W2291 order-routing exception, VS-56 / W2198 tracking) — the exception detection and resolution
- DC coordination (links to VS-04 / W3, W106 dispatch) — the re-delivery coordination
- Customer comms (links to VS-13 / W56) — the exception-customer notification

steps.activity: Coordinator categorizes: delay, damage, wrong items, failed delivery, breakdown; resolves: re-delivery, replacement, escalation to 3PL, coordination with DC

Automation Opportunity: - Routes auto-generated; real-time-traffic-adjusted; Supervisor exceptions only
Controls: - CTL-398 (ensure controlled execution — Delivery Performance & SLA Management (PA-56.2).)
- CTL-398 (route-optimization accuracy); operational: Logistics Manager daily sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Optimization-vs-reality-divergence risk**: the optimized route doesn't account for real-time road conditions (traffic, construction); mitigated by the Supervisor's manual adjustment and the real-time traffic feed
- **Over-optimization risk**: too many stops per route saves cost but delays the last-stop customer; mitigated by the stops-per-route cap
System Touchpoints: - Route optimization (links to VS-06 / W196 route planning, W199 telematics) — the route engine
- DC dispatch (links to VS-04 / W106 dispatch, W585 dock scheduling) — the dispatch coordination
- Order management (links to VS-60 / W536) — the delivery-order source
Time Estimate: ~1.5 hours/day × 4 DCs = **~1,500 hours/year** DC Dispatch Supervisors.

steps.activity: System generates optimized routes: groups by geography, minimizes distance, balances capacity; Supervisor reviews and adjusts for priorities, last-minute orders, road closures

Automation Opportunity: - Peak-volume auto-forecasted; capacity-need auto-computed; peak-rate-agreement auto-referenced
Controls: - CTL-398 (ensure controlled execution — Delivery Performance & SLA Management (PA-56.2).)
- CTL-398 (capacity-plan accuracy); operational: VP Supply Chain sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-shortfall risk**: the peak exceeds the pre-booked capacity; mitigated by the 4–6 week pre-booking and the temporary-driver/DC-overtime surge plan
- **Peak-rate-cost risk**: surge rates (peak premium) inflate the delivery cost; mitigated by the annual peak-rate agreement (locked-in rate vs. spot premium)
System Touchpoints: - Capacity forecasting (links to VS-56 / W2195 capacity planning, VS-60 / W2307) — the peak-volume forecast
- 3PL capacity (links to VS-56 / W2190 partner onboarding, W2193 rate card) — the surge capacity pre-booking
- DC scheduling (links to VS-04 / W585) — the extended windows
Time Estimate: ~2 weeks/peak × 2.5 + ~2.5 days post-peak = **~200 hours/year** Logistics Manager.

steps.activity: Manager forecasts peak volume; pre-books 3PL capacity 4–6 weeks ahead; implements surge plan: extended windows, additional routes, temporary drivers, DC overtime
Post-peak: analyzes vs. plan; adjusts for next peak; updates contracts with peak rate agreements
